result.title: AdaptRouter: Adaptive Routing across Evolving Tasks and Models
result.summary: Model routing assigns each query to a suitable foundation model, but tasks and available models keep changing, and existing routers are either untrained for the pool at hand or fit once and forget earlier tasks when updated. We present AdaptRouter, an adaptive router trained by policy learning: a compact multimodal decision model reads each question with cards describing the current experts and learns from native task feedback, without routing labels, to select one frozen expert. Open-weight and API experts share the router, its inputs, and the quality-cost trade-off but use different losses: cheap open-weight experts are explored with RL, whereas paid API experts are queried once and their cached feedback is reused as soft labels. New tasks are learned without replay, new experts enter as cards, and an open-weight quality-first advantage provably keeps cost from overriding quality. Across four task stages, AdaptRouter loses at most 0.4 points on earlier tasks, whereas feedback-trained routers lose up to 7.0, and as its pool grows from three to ten experts, its accuracy rises from 67.2% to 72.1%. On five API models, it exceeds GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra (low) by over 22 points at under a third of their cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AdaptRouter，用策略学习训练一个紧凑多模态决策模型，读取问题与描述当前可用专家的卡片，在无路由标签、仅依赖任务原生反馈的条件下为每个查询选择一个冻结专家；并支持新任务无回放增量学习、开放权重与 API 专家混合的质量-成本权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按成本-质量权衡选择外部计算资源的元决策框架，可能与 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的计算分配与停止判断形成概念类比；但作用对象是模型路由而非 latent 视觉推理状态，可供核查迁移价值有限。
